parts.title: Part 1 · Short texts
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: Zara should
questions.explanation: Ali says he has to work late and will eat at work. Zara should therefore have dinner without him, rather than buy or prepare food for him.
questions.evidence: I'll eat at work.

questions.prompt: What does the seller say?
questions.explanation: The table top has some damage, so the furniture is not all in perfect condition. The seller can only be contacted after 7 p.m.
questions.evidence: Some damage to table top.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct meaning of the tennis equipment notice.
questions.explanation: The notice limits use of this tennis equipment to club members. Asking at Reception is the way for members to hire it, not an invitation for non-members to use it.
questions.evidence: This tennis equipment is for club members only.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct meaning of Olivia’s message.
questions.explanation: Olivia is unwell but encourages Aiden to attend the running club without her. She reassures him that the group is helpful to new members.
questions.evidence: But you should definitely go, even though it’s your first time.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct statement about the college art class.
questions.explanation: Students must research famous landscape paintings before the next lesson so they can discuss them. Looking at pictures on computers does not mean they must create digital paintings.
questions.evidence: find out about famous landscape paintings so you can discuss them in class.

parts.title: Part 2 · Matching
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer. Match each person to the most suitable option. There are three extra options.

questions.prompt: Alan is keen on history, and wants to visit a castle that was the site of well-known historical events. He’d like the castle to be near the coast, with tours led by a guide.
questions.explanation: Carston Castle has expert-led tours, a history of famous battles and views of the sea. These match Alan’s interest in historical events and his wish for a guided coastal visit.
questions.evidence: Hear how the building was once the scene of famous battles

questions.prompt: Yoshiko wants to see a castle that people are still living in. She loves visiting beautiful gardens, and would like to explore interesting places in the castle.
questions.explanation: Durston Castle is still the Durston family’s home. It also offers attractive gardens, secret tunnels and unusual underground rooms for Yoshiko to explore.
questions.evidence: Because the building is the Durston family’s home

questions.prompt: Paulo and Maria collect antiques, so want to visit a castle that still has some of its original furniture on display, and hear about the building’s history. They also want something that’s particularly suitable for young children.
questions.explanation: Sawbridge Castle displays furniture used by its former residents and provides recorded historical information through headphones. Its toy museum also gives their young children something suitable to enjoy.
questions.evidence: Visitors of all ages will love the toy museum in the gardens.

questions.prompt: Kerim wants somewhere with a great historical atmosphere, with typical food from the past to try, and people dressed in costume. He’d also like to see art that’s been in the castle for centuries.
questions.explanation: Castle Woodward recreates the past through staff costumes and food made from historical recipes. Its original paintings of former residents also satisfy Kerim’s interest in old art.
questions.evidence: the walls are covered with original paintings of the generations of people who’ve lived in the castle.

questions.prompt: Jake and his brother have always wanted to visit the ruins of a castle surrounded by water, with great views. Jake also wants to learn about wildlife living in and around the castle.
questions.explanation: Only parts of Marlin Castle remain, and it stands in a lake with views from a high tower. Talks about its bats, birds and butterflies provide the wildlife information Jake wants.
questions.evidence: The castle is in the middle of a lake and has lovely gardens.

parts.title: Part 3 · Long text
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: What helped Ana stop being scared of singing to an audience?
questions.explanation: Joining the school theatre club helped Ana gain confidence. After attending it, she was able to sing happily at the end-of-term concert.
questions.evidence: joining the school theatre club might make her more confident.

questions.prompt: How was the songwriting course useful for Ana?
questions.explanation: Ana felt ignored by the course teacher, and that frustration inspired Something to Say. The course was useful because it gave her a subject for a song.
questions.evidence: she wrote Something to Say about how annoyed this made her feel.

questions.prompt: Ana decided to work with Joss Alton because
questions.explanation: Ana initially worried that the company would tell her what to sing. Joss reassured her that this would not happen, so she agreed to work with him.
questions.evidence: didn’t want someone telling her what to sing. However, Joss persuaded her this wouldn’t happen

questions.prompt: Ana most enjoys writing songs that
questions.explanation: Ana says difficult periods give her more to write about than happy ones. Her example of Decision also concerns an upsetting personal experience.
questions.evidence: when it’s not, there’s more for her to say.

questions.prompt: What would Ana write to fans in her blog?
questions.explanation: Ana was delighted by online comments from people who loved the song and found new meanings in its words. This supports the blog message about valuing listeners who pay close attention to her songs.
questions.evidence: found new meanings in the words each time they heard them.

parts.title: Part 4 · Missing sentences
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer. Five sentences have been removed from the text. There are three extra sentences which you do not need to use.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence for gap 16 in Steve Dalway’s cycle ride.
questions.explanation: The previous sentence lists services provided by the organising company. E adds its food and drink stops, and the following phrase “Even with these” refers to those helpful stops.
questions.evidence: It also arranged stops every 50 km for snacks and drinks.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence for gap 17 in Steve Dalway’s cycle ride.
questions.explanation: Steve’s previous long ride in Europe meant he already knew what a demanding ride would involve. A makes that connection and leads naturally into the example about eating properly.
questions.evidence: He therefore had an idea of what to expect on this one.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence for gap 18 in Steve Dalway’s cycle ride.
questions.explanation: “Doing that” refers to eating a large breakfast each morning. D explains why this habit mattered: it supplied the energy Steve needed to continue cycling.
questions.evidence: Doing that gave him the energy he needed to keep going.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence for gap 19 in Steve Dalway’s cycle ride.
questions.explanation: The passage has just described the difficult mountain climb. H introduces additional challenges, followed by the example of extreme heat in the Mojave desert.
questions.evidence: There were other challenges, too.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence for gap 20 in Steve Dalway’s cycle ride.
questions.explanation: The map showed the route for the following day and also how far the riders had already travelled. B explains this second purpose, which the next sentence illustrates through the slowly advancing black line.
questions.evidence: It also allowed them to see the progress they had made.

parts.title: Part 5 · Multiple-choice cloze
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 21 in Honey.
questions.explanation: “Common food” means a food that is familiar and widely eaten. This fits the opening statement that people all over the world enjoy honey.
questions.evidence: People all over the world enjoy eating honey.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 22 in Honey.
questions.explanation: The flowers visited influence the honey’s taste and colour, so “affects” is the verb with the right meaning. The singular subject “type” also agrees with “affects”.
questions.evidence: both how the honey tastes and its colour.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 23 in Honey.
questions.explanation: “Actually” introduces a fact that may surprise the reader: there are over three hundred kinds of honey. The other adverbs do not fit this use.
questions.evidence: more than three hundred kinds of honey.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 24 in Honey.
questions.explanation: “In ancient times” is the expression for the distant past. It suits the explanation that honey was used before sugar became common.
questions.evidence: honey was added to food instead of sugar, as sugar was very rare.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 25 in Honey.
questions.explanation: We use “cure” with illnesses or health problems. “Mend” and “repair” normally describe fixing objects, while “assist” does not mean making a health problem better.
questions.evidence: various health problems.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 26 in Honey.
questions.explanation: “Nowadays” means at the present time. It contrasts modern use of honey with the practices in ancient times described just before it.
questions.evidence: people all over the world still add it to hot water

parts.title: Part 6 · Open cloze
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer. Write one word for each gap.

questions.prompt: Starting at college: I was ______ nervous that I couldn’t even ask anyone for help.
questions.explanation: The structure “so + adjective + that” describes a degree that causes a result. Emma was so nervous that she could not ask for help.
questions.evidence: nervous that I couldn’t even ask anyone for help.

questions.prompt: Starting at college: Remember that ______ student at the college has been new at one time.
questions.explanation: Both “every student” and “each student” mean all the students considered individually. A singular word is needed before “student” and the singular verb “has”.
questions.evidence: student at the college has been new at one time

questions.prompt: Starting at college: So ______ you’re not sure where to go, just ask.
questions.explanation: “If” introduces the situation in which a student should ask for help. “When” and “whenever” also fit, meaning on occasions when the student is unsure.
questions.evidence: you’re not sure where to go, just ask

questions.prompt: Starting at college: To make some friends, ______ not spend break times with some of your new classmates in the café?
questions.explanation: “Why not” is a standard way to make a suggestion. Emma is suggesting spending breaks with classmates as a way to make friends.
questions.evidence: not spend break times with some of your new classmates in the café?

questions.prompt: Starting at college: Or how ______ joining one of the many clubs we have at the college?
questions.explanation: The suggestion pattern is “How about + -ing”. “About” therefore comes before “joining”.
questions.evidence: joining one of the many clubs we have at the college?

questions.prompt: Starting at college: ______ are lots to choose from.
questions.explanation: “There are” introduces the existence of many clubs. “There” is required before the plural verb “are”.
questions.evidence: are lots to choose from.
